transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lucas Martin (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (Nimbus Head of Platform), Aisha Rahman (CTO), Tom Wu (SRE), Rita Solis (PM)

Summary: quick sync on POC results and integration friction points. Focus on SDK usage for tool/function calls and producing structured JSON output from the model. Review of perf numbers (latency/cost), discussion of KV cache and batching, SSO/security ask, and next steps for exec demo and benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: All right good morning everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the numbers from last week's run.
[00:14] Carlos: hey Jordan, morning. we did a quick smoke last night, a few questions after the run.
[00:20] Priya: morning — i'll share the latest benchmark sheet in chat after, it includes median p95, token cost approximations. some notes about the SDK flags we recommended.
[00:34] Aisha: thanks, appreciate. security team will want the SSO and audit log details before exec demo.
[00:40] Jordan: noted, we'll send the SSO checklist and SOC2 docs. lucas is copied and will help.

Topics: Results review; SDK integration errors; function/tool calling patterns; structured output schema; tuning (batching, kv cache, quantization); security/SSO; next steps.

[05:05] Priya: ok first — results review. last week you ran the 1k-message sample end-to-end. median latency with hosted model was ~240ms per request, p95 about 680ms. when we enabled continuous batching with batch size up to 8 it moved median to 210ms but p95 didn't change much, which suggests a single long tail request. also cost per 1k requests estimated at $12.3 with current tokenization.
[05:37] Tom: yeah we saw some spikes, especially with messages that have long context (over 1k tokens) — those were the p95. any config to drop those?
[05:46] Priya: two levers — enable prefix KV caching for repeated user-system turns, and set max_seq_len/clipping on the SDK to truncate non-essential context. both will reduce compute for the heavy ones. also quantized model variants cut token cost roughly 30% in our internal runs, but we'll want to validate hallucination/regression risk on your prompts.
[06:12] Carlos: good. we need to guard against quality regressions, finance will not accept output drift.
[06:20] Priya: totally understood — we'll tie the quantized run to your prompt test-suite (you provided the 200 prompt set). we'll run A/B and give confusion matrices.

SDK integration notes
[09:00] Jordan: can you walk through the SDK flow you're using for function/tool calls? we want to make sure the client is calling the right endpoints and handling structured responses.
[09:10] Tom: sure, currently using the Node SDK, send createCompletion with inputs and a tools array, then parse the toolResponse. we've seen a few malformed JSON returns when the model output includes explanatory text before the JSON block.
[09:32] Priya: yep that's common. two patterns to reduce that: 1) use the structured_output schema enforcement flag in the SDK (we'll share exact param name), it forces model to return strict JSON or retries; 2) wrap the function call invocation using tool_call wrapper — this prompts the model to emit a single top-level tool_response object. both are in our SDK docs (https://redwood.ai/sdk -> note: doc link placeholder).
[10:05] Tom: example we tried — model returned 'Here's the result:' followed by JSON, and our parser choked. is there a built-in sanitizer?
[10:12] Priya: the SDK has a parser with lenient mode by default which strips leading tokens, but when you need strong guarantees set strict_json: true and the SDK will request a regeneration on violations. there's also a streaming mode that yields structured events so you can handle partial tool outputs.

Structured output schema discussion
[12:30] Rita: our product needs a canonical payload: {action_type, account_id, amount, confidence, metadata}. we want minimal post-processing.
[12:42] Priya: perfect. we recommended using the schema parameter with required fields. the model will then validate and return either 'valid_schema' object or an 'error' with path. small caveat — schema enforcement adds 5-10% latency in our tests due to extra validation loops.
[13:03] Carlos: acceptable if it reduces downstream parsing. finance wants confidence scores too.
[13:10] Priya: we can include a float confidence field and an explainability token. also the SDK can attach request_id headers so you can trace tokens back to logs in console.

[16:45] Jordan: on private deployment or dedicated capacity question — Carlos asked about bringing the POC to dedicated GPUs if throughput grows. pricing and commitment questions?
[16:56] Carlos: yes — if we need guaranteed throughput for peak business hours. what's the uplift vs hosted?
[17:05] Jordan: quick numbers — dedicated pool pricing example is in the deck we'll send; rough uplift 2.5x vs hosted per-token baseline but you get predictable latency and capacity and a soft SLA. we'll include burst options and overage policies.
[17:25] Aisha: ok include sample TCO for 6 months with our 100k monthly messages.

Errors and debugging
[20:00] Tom: logs — when we hit malformed JSON, what logs should we pull and share?
[20:07] Priya: capture the SDK debug log (enable DEBUG env var), the raw response body, and the request_id header. also, if using streaming, include event order. we'll give a triage doc.
[20:30] Tom: will do.

Security asks
[23:00] Aisha: our security team requires SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 2 years, and KMS-managed keys for private deployment. do you support that?
[23:15] Jordan: yes — we support SAML/SCIM provisioning for enterprise, audit logs with configurable retention on Dedicated/Private, and KMS integrations. Lucas will share the security pack and a checklist.
[23:34] Aisha: great, also need contract language for data residency — we operate in US-only region for payments data.
[23:42] Jordan: noted — we'll surface applicable clauses and region options.

Demo and next steps recap
[30:00] Jordan: recap — Priya will run the 2k-message benchmark with KV caching and quantized variant on the sample prompts and share results. Jordan will send pricing deck, SSO/SOC2 security pack, and sample TCO. Tom will validate SDK strict_json/structured_output flags and share logs for any failures. Rita to confirm stakeholders. We will aim to have an exec demo week of 2026-08-31 pending security review.
[30:35] Carlos: that works. one ask — can we get a short checklist for what the security team needs to see before the exec demo?
[30:44] Lucas: yes i'll send a one-pager checklist with the pack.

[33:22] Priya: quick note on tuning — when you enable KV cache, set cache window to 3-6 turns initially, it keeps correctness while saving compute. also if you have repeated system prompts we recommend storing system role in client to avoid resending and pushing to cache.
[33:46] Tom: good tip, we'll try.

[36:00] Rita: small UX question — structured output with confidence, if confidence < 0.6 we want the model to flag for manual review. can sdk easily support a rule engine?
[36:12] Priya: SDK can surface the confidence and you can wire a small rule in the client; we also offer built-in routing to a fallback model or human-in-the-loop via our console rules API (we'll share the doc snippet).

Closing
[40:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the benchmark sheet and security docs by EOD 2026-08-21. any final questions?
[40:08] Aisha: none from me.
[40:12] Carlos: no, thanks.
[40:15] Tom: thanks.
[40:18] Rita: thanks all.

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/sdk (SDK docs placeholder), shared benchmark spreadsheet (link in chat), security pack PDF (sent after meeting).

End of transcript.
